subject: F3 key does not switch to TMB mode in AD Studio

messages.author: df0cc20f0eeb00d0
messages.subject: F3 key does not switch to TMB mode in AD Studio
parts:
I am trying to become familiar with Template Model Builder TMB and AD Model Builder ADMB in AD Studio which uses Emacs. I have been working through the user's guide AD Studio: Statistical modelling in ADMB and TMB Version 1.0 (2018-01-22) by Arni Magnusson. I can follow the initial section of the guide focusing on ADMB and the examples run as expected. However, once the guide switches to TMB I encounter a problem. The guide says to press F3 to switch to tmb-mode. However, when I press F3 on my Dell XPS 15 (9570) laptop with Windows 10 the only option offered is to adjust the volume of the laptop's speakers. Apparently if I did manage to switch to tmb-mode I eventually would need to press F2 to switch back to admb-mode. But pressing the F2 key only allows me to adjust the speaker volume as well. Indeed the F2 and F3 keys on my laptop even include a small speaker icon.

Is there an alternative method of accessing tmb-mode in AD Studio? Or perhaps is there a way to switch the laptop's F3 key functionality to activate tmb-mode and the F2 key to activate admb-mode?  I have installed R in c:\gnu\r and have installed the TMB R package. The tmb.el file is located in C:\~\emacs\lisp\tmb.


Earlier I asked this question on the (emacs) Exchange here:


https://emacs.stackexchange.com/questions/59096/f3-key-does-not-switch-to-tmb-mode-in-ad-studio


Then I discovered the following work around:


I had previously noticed that if I double-clicked on an example ADMB file, eg. simple.tpl, then AD Studio would open in ADMB mode. So, I located an example TMB file, simple.cpp, found here: C:\~\R\win-library\4.0\TMB\examples. I moved simple.cpp and simple.R to a new folder C:\demo. When I double-clicked on simple.cpp then AD Studio opened in TMB mode. If I double-clicked on simple.R then AD Studio opened in lmenu-R mode.

So, it appears I can go from one mode to another by clicking on an external file associated with the mode of interest. This is probably good enough. Although being able to switch modes from within AD Studio would seem to be more convenient.

I was able to obtain parameter estimates from simple.R but a few additional questions arose in the process.  I should probably post those other questions separately.

Thank you for any advice regarding switching modes from within AD Studio.

Mark

messages.subject: Re: F3 key does not switch to TMB mode in AD Studio
parts: My Dell XPS 15 9570 laptop comes with an 'Fn' key.  If I press this 'Fn' key + the 'F2' key (or the 'Fn' key + the 'F3' key) then AD Studio will switch modes.
